title: Step 1 - Text Classification Using Bag-of-Words and Random Forest in R

cues.en: Instructor: Hello and welcome to this tutorial, and mostly, welcome to part seven, Natural Language Processing.
cues.zh: 講師：大家好，歡迎來到教學，更歡迎來到第七部分「自然語言處理」。

cues.en: So what is Natural Language Processing all about?
Well, it's about analyzing texts.
These texts can be books, reviews, some HTML webpages that you extract from web scrapping, all sorts of texts.
cues.zh: 可以是書、評論、網路爬取的 HTML 網頁，各類文字。

cues.en: And therefore, Natural Language Processing is a branch of machine learning, where we do some predictive analysis on texts mostly.
cues.zh: 所以是主要對文字做預測分析的機器學習分支。

cues.en: So in this part, these texts are going to be reviews, you know, written reviews of restaurants.
cues.zh: 這部分是餐廳書面評論。

cues.en: And so we will make some machine learning models that will predict if the review is positive or negative.
cues.zh: 建立模型，預測正面或負面。

cues.en: So, this is a simple example of application of Natural Language Processing, but the algorithm will make in this part, will be very well applicable to other kinds of texts.
cues.zh: 這是簡單應用，但建立的演算法也能套其他文字。

cues.en: You know you'll be able to apply this on books, for example, to predict the genre of a book.
You know whether a book is a thriller, a comedy or a romance.
You'll be also able to use it on HTML webpages to do whatever kind of analysis you wanna do on these pages.
cues.zh: 也可對 HTML 網頁做想要的分析。

cues.en: You can also apply it on newspapers you know to predict in which category an article belongs to.
cues.zh: 報紙也能，預測文章類別。

cues.en: Well, you'll see that we'll make a general model that you'll be able to apply on most of the texts.
cues.zh: 會建一般模型，適用多數文字。

cues.en: And of course, if you need to apply this on a more complicated text, you can ask me some questions in the Q and A, and I'll tell you what to add to make this code work properly for your problem, your text.
cues.zh: 若需更複雜文字，在問答區問，我會說明怎麼補充，讓程式適用問題與文字。

cues.en: Okay, so let's start this.
Let's start our algorithm.
And before starting with the first code section let's do the basic step.
cues.zh: 第一個程式區段前，先基本步驟。

cues.en: Let's set the right folder as working directory.
So we'll go to our machine learning AZ folder then part seven, Natural Language Processing.
cues.zh: 到 Machine Learning A-Z、第七部分 NLP。

cues.en: So congratulations for reaching the part you are now entering into a very useful and exciting branch of machine learning.
cues.zh: 恭喜走到這裡，進入實用、精彩的分支。

cues.en: So let's go in there.
And now we have to pick the section natural language processing. So here we go.
That's the folder we wanna set as working directory.
cues.zh: 就是要設為工作目錄的資料夾。

cues.en: So now we'll click on this more button here and then set as working directory.
All good.
And now as you can notice in this folder that we just set it as working directory, we have two data files.
cues.zh: 這個資料夾有兩個資料檔。

cues.en: We have a restaurant reviews dot CSV file and a restaurant reviews dot tsv file.
So I left these two data files on purpose because there is an important thing to understand when we prepare text data sets that I would like to highlight and show you right now.
cues.zh: 刻意留兩檔，因為準備文字資料集有個重點，現在要說明。

cues.en: So I'm gonna go to my folder on my computer and we'll have a look at these two files from there.
So right now I'm going to my folder.
Here it is.
And let's open the two restroom reviews csv.
So open with text edit, here we go.
And restroom reviews dot tsv.
So same open with text edits.
So that's the CSV and that's the tsv.
Let's first have a look at the csv.
As you can see the first line here is the title of the future columns we're gonna have in our studio.
cues.zh: 第一列是 RStudio 裡未來欄位標題。

cues.en: The first column is review, and the second column is light.
cues.zh: 第一欄 Review，第二欄 Liked。

cues.en: And I can see that because these two terms here are separated by a comma, and this is a CSV file meaning that all the columns are separated by a comma.
cues.zh: 知道是因為以逗號分隔；CSV 各欄都用逗號。

cues.en: So that's the first line containing the titles of the columns.
cues.zh: 這是含欄標題的第一列。

cues.en: And then we have all our observations.
So one line corresponds to one observation.
And as you can see in each of these lines we first have the review.
So this is of course a review of a restaurant.
So wow, love this place.
Meaning of course, that the review is positive.
And therefore, in the second column, the liked column we have a one here meaning that the review is indeed positive.
cues.zh: 所以第二欄 Liked 是 1，表示正評。

cues.en: So the variable for this liked column can take two values one or zero, and one means that it's a positive review and zero means that it's a negative review.
cues.zh: Liked 可取 1 或 0，1 正、0 負。

cues.en: So indeed, as you can see in the second review crust is not good.
cues.zh: 第二則 Crust is not good，餅皮不好。

cues.en: Well, of course that's a negative review and therefore there is a zero here.
All right, so that's actually the kind of file we're used to because since the beginning of this course, we've only been using some CSV file where the columns are separated
cues.zh: 這是熟悉檔案，本課開始一直用逗號分欄的

cues.en: by a comma, but here we have something different.
We can see that we have the same columns.
First column is review, second column is liked and we have the same reviews.
cues.zh: 第一 Review、第二 Liked，評論也相同。

cues.en: So these are exactly the same data sets with the same data.
But there is one major difference.
And as you might have guessed this difference is the delimiter and this file here, the delimiter is a comma.
cues.zh: 猜得到，是分隔符號。這檔用逗號。

cues.en: So that's the delimiter separating the two columns.
And in this file, the delimiter is a tab and that's why we call it tsv, tab separated values vs CSV comma separated values.
cues.zh: 另一檔用 Tab，所以叫 TSV 定位字元分隔值，相對 CSV 逗號分隔值。

cues.en: And so now according to you which one should we choose for our future algorithm?
cues.zh: 未來演算法應該選哪個？

cues.en: You know, we'll have a machine learning algorithm analyzing all the reviews here.
And then the goal of this algorithm will be to predict whether the review is positive or negative.
All right.
But now the question is do we need a data set where the columns are separated by a comma or by a tab?
cues.zh: 問題是，資料集欄用逗號還是 Tab 分開？

cues.en: Well, the answer is, as you might have guessed by a tab.
And why is that?
It's because we already have some commas in the reviews itself.
Well, for example, this one, this review is, the food comma amazing.
So if we use our CSV file where the delimiter is a comma well we'll have a problem for this review here because for this particular observation the first column will contain the food here.
cues.zh: 若用逗號分隔 CSV，這筆有問題，第一欄只有 The food。

cues.en: So R will think it's a review the food and the second column will not be one here but amazing because there is this comma here that is taken
cues.zh: R 以為評論是 The food，第二欄不是 1，而是 amazing，因為逗號被視為

cues.en: for the delimiter and therefore it will separate the food and amazing.
cues.zh: 分隔符，分開 The food 和 amazing。

cues.en: And therefore, what will happen to one it will go to the next observation and therefore one will be taken for a new review.
cues.zh: 那 1 會怎樣？到下一筆，成為新評論。

cues.en: So that will not make any sense.
And this will mess up with the whole algorithm.
And that's why it's way better to take tabs here because you know when people write reviews they do not put tabs in the review.
cues.zh: 所以用 Tab 好得多，因為寫評論不會放 Tab。

cues.en: Well, that would be very rare.
They would put comma very easily as we can see for this particular review.
cues.zh: 逗號很容易出現，像這則。

cues.en: And we can find other reviews with commas, I'm sure of it.
Yes indeed.
We have another one here.
This place is not worth your time, comma, let alone Vegas.
cues.zh: 「這地方不值得你花時間，更別說在 Vegas。」中間逗號。

cues.en: So it's very natural to put some commas in the reviews but not much natural to put some tabs in the reviews.
cues.zh: 評論放逗號很自然，Tab 不自然。

cues.en: And besides if you press on tab when you're writing a review well this will go to the next, you know button to like submit your review or something else.
cues.zh: 而且寫評論時按 Tab，會到下一個按鈕，例如送出。

cues.en: But by pressing the tab button when you're writing your review you would get out of the review and you would not be able to continue to write it.
cues.zh: 按 Tab 會跳離評論，無法繼續寫。

cues.en: So we will never find a tab in the review and that's why we will never have this problem of getting this anomalies due
cues.zh: 所以不會遇到 Tab，也就不會有這種因為單則評論內重複

cues.en: to duplicate delimiters in one specific review.
So I really recommend to prepare your text data sets this way with a tab separator because you will never have that kind of problem.
cues.zh: 很建議用 Tab 準備文字資料集，避免這種問題。

cues.en: One other solution if you really want to use a CSV would be to include some double quotes here one at the left of the review and one at the right.
cues.zh: 如果一定要 CSV，另一解法是在評論左右加雙引號。

cues.en: But you would still get some problems in case you have some double quotes in the reviews itself.
cues.zh: 但評論本身有雙引號，仍會遇問題。

cues.en: I'm sure we can find one.
Let's have a look.
Let's press command F to find a double quote.
cues.zh: Command 加 F 找雙引號。

cues.en: Here we are.
And that's exactly what I'm talking about.
For example, let's have a look at this review here.
The description said yum, yum sauce.
Well that's because this person here is quoting a description found somewhere.
cues.zh: 因為此人引用別處描述。

cues.en: And so since it's quoting it's using some double quotes here, Yum, yum sauce.
cues.zh: 引用時使用雙引號包 Yum Yum 醬。

cues.en: And another one here.
So even if you put some double quotes to separate your reviews from the result that is one or zero well you would still have this kind of problem, whereas
cues.zh: 所以即使用雙引號分開評論與 1、0 結果，仍可能有這問題；

cues.en: if you separate your review in the liked variable by a tab you will never get this kind of problem because no one will press tab by writing a review.
cues.zh: 但評論與 Liked 用 Tab，就不會，因為寫評論沒人按 Tab。

cues.en: So definitely that's the one we'll go for.
Restaurant underscore reviews dot tsv tab separated values.
And by the way, this is a data set taken from a paper from group to individual labels using deep features by code.
cues.zh: 順帶一提，資料集來自論文 From Group to Individual Labels Using Deep Features，作者 Kotzias 等人。

cues.en: So we will use this data set and this contains 1000 reviews.
And for each of the review we have the real results, zero or one.
So let's do it.
Let's start implementing our algorithm and we will start with the first step that is to import this data set restaurant reviews dot tsv into our studio.
cues.zh: 實作第一步，把 Restaurant_Reviews.tsv 匯入 RStudio。

cues.en: So let's do it.
Let's close this and let's go back to our studio.
All right, so now let's import the dataset.
So as usual, we're gonna call our dataset dataset this way and then equals, and then that's where we use a function to import the dataset.
cues.zh: 照慣例叫 dataset，等於，再用匯入函式。

cues.en: However, so far we've been using the re dot CSV function to import our data sets because simply our data sets were CSV files.
cues.zh: 到目前一直 read.csv，因為檔案都是 CSV。

cues.en: But as we just understood this time we're not dealing with a CSV file, we are dealing with a TSV file.
cues.zh: 但這次不是 CSV，是 TSV。

cues.en: So of course things might be different now but we will still type read dot csv here and then some parenthesis.
cues.zh: 當然可能不同，但先輸入 read.csv，加括號。

cues.en: And then let's press F1 here to get some info about this re dot CSV function.
So what do we see?
First, we see that we don't only have one import function.
cues.zh: 首先不只一個匯入函式。

cues.en: Indeed, we can see here that we have the re dot table function which we haven't used yet.
The re dot CSV function which is the function we've been using since the beginning of this course.
Then we also have the re dot CSV two function which is the same as this one with the only difference that the default separator you know, the delimiter that is separating your columns
cues.zh: 也有 read.csv2，基本相同，唯一差別是預設分隔符號，

cues.en: is a semi colon instead of a comma as the default parameter for the re dot CSV function.
cues.zh: 改分號，不是 read.csv 預設的逗號。

cues.en: So that's the main difference between the two.
But that's not what we are interested in right now because we would like to use a function where the default parameter for the separator is a tab and not a semi colon.
cues.zh: 但目前要的不是它，希望預設是 Tab，不是分號。

cues.en: We could still use this re dot series function and change the set parameter, but you know let's use another function for once to import the dataset with the right default parameter.
cues.zh: 也能繼續 read.csv 再改 sep，但這次用另一個預設正確的函式。

cues.en: And speaking of this default parameter which should be the tab separator well that's actually the next import function which is the read dot dilem function.
cues.zh: 說到預設 Tab，下一個 read.delim 就是。

cues.en: Indeed, you can see here that the default parameter for the separator is a tab slash t here means tab actually.
cues.zh: 可以看到 sep 預設是 Tab，反斜線 t 代表 Tab。

cues.en: So that's exactly the function we want.
That's the best function to use for our data set right now because our data set contains columns separated by a tab.
cues.zh: 最適合目前各欄 Tab 分隔的資料集。

cues.en: So that's the function we'll use.
So I'm going to remove here read dot csv and replace it by re dot delim.
Here we go.
And now we input the parameters.
So it's the same principle as for re dot csv.
We of course need to input first the data set in quotes.
cues.zh: 先輸入引號包住的檔名。

cues.en: And the data set is called restaurant reviews dot tsv.
So we need to specify this because indeed in our working directory folder, we have the two files, CSV and tsv.
cues.zh: 必須指定，因為工作目錄兩檔 CSV、TSV 都有。

cues.en: So we need to specify here, tsv, that's the first parameter.
cues.zh: 這裡指定 TSV，第一個參數。

cues.en: And then we have some other parameters like this head of parameter here which is by default equals to true, meaning that it considers the first line of our data set as the titles of the columns
cues.zh: 再有 header，預設 TRUE，把第一行視為欄標題，

cues.en: which is the case for our data set.
Because remember the first line is review tab liked and review is the title of the first column and liked is the title of the second column.
cues.zh: 記得第一行 Review、Tab、Liked，分別是第一、第二欄標題。

cues.en: So we are good with this head of parameter so we don't need to input this.
cues.zh: 所以 header 沒問題，不必輸入。

cues.en: And same for this next parameter set because by default the parameter for the separator is a tab and that's exactly what we need right now.
cues.zh: sep 也一樣，預設 Tab，正是需要。

cues.en: And then we have this parameter quote and that's a very useful parameter to input for Natural Language Processing because most of the time you'll find some quotes
cues.zh: 接著 quote，NLP 很有用，因為文字常有引號，

cues.en: most of the time double quotes in your text.
we checked that we had some in our reviews, and so we need to ignore these quotes because we don't want to have some kind of misinterpretation when our re dot delim function reads all the reviews.
cues.zh: 確認評論有引號，要忽略，避免 read.delim 讀評論時誤解。

cues.en: So in general, in Natural Language Processing it's better to ignore any kind of quotes.
cues.zh: 通常 NLP 忽略各種引號比較好。

cues.en: We did exactly the same in Python and everything went well.
So we'll do the same here.
And to do this, we add this quote parameter and we said it equals to actually nothing in quotes.
You know, by putting nothing in this quote here, that means that it's ignoring any kind of quotes in the text.
cues.zh: 引號裡不放任何東西，表示忽略文字裡各種引號。

cues.en: So that's good.
And now we'll add a last parameter that is not specified here and which is the strings as factors parameter.
cues.zh: 最後加這裡沒顯示的 stringsAsFactors。

cues.en: And what is this parameter used for?
Well, you know, the first column of our data set contains the written reviews and you know in R when we're making some classification models which will be what we'll be doing here
cues.zh: 第一欄是文字評論，R 裡做分類，也就是這裡 NLP，

cues.en: in Natural Language Processing because basically we'll be classifying new reviews and tell whether they are positive or negative.
cues.zh: 會分類新評論，判斷正面負面。

cues.en: So that's classification.
And you know, when we're doing some classification models and working with some categorical variables well remember we use this factor function to specify the categorical variables as factors.
cues.zh: 分類模型處理類別變數時，記得用 factor 指定為因子。

cues.en: And you know, right now we have some reviews.
And since in some way it's not a numeric variable, you know taking some continuous real values, well, in some way it can be considered as a categorical variable
cues.zh: 不是連續實數的數值變數，某種程度可視為類別變數，

cues.en: having some different factors.
But in Natural Language Processing, we must not identify the reviews as factors in R.
cues.zh: 但 NLP 裡，不能把評論當 R 因子。

cues.en: And that's because we will analyze the inside of the reviews because we'll be analyzing the different words of the review to understand the correlations between the presence of the words and the result
cues.zh: 因為要分析內部，分析各詞，理解詞的出現與

cues.en: whether the review is positive or negative.
So since we'll drill into the review and analyze its content, well, we must not specify the review as factors as if it was a single entity
cues.zh: 既然要深入評論內容，就不能當成單一實體的因子，

cues.en: because that's what a factor would be, a single entity having a single meaning regardless of the different meanings of the different words of the review.
cues.zh: 因子是一個單一意義的實體，不考慮評論中各詞意義。

cues.en: And so to prevent from identifying those reviews as factors well what we need to do is add this other parameter which is the string as factors parameter.
cues.zh: 避免評論被當因子，就加 stringsAsFactors。

cues.en: Here it is, I just need to press enter.
And now, now we just need to input false like this not in quotes and that will not identify the reviews as factors.
cues.zh: 只要輸入 FALSE，不加引號，就不當因子。

cues.en: And that's all.
That's how we should import this text file.
cues.zh: 這是匯入文字檔的方式。

cues.en: You know, using the re delim import function to import a TSV file by default and then add this quote parameter to ignore the quotes and then add this string, it's factors parameter to prevent
cues.zh: read.delim 預設匯入 TSV，quote 忽略引號，再 stringsAsFactors 避免

cues.en: from identifying the reviews as factors.
All right, so let's do it.
Let's select this line of code and execute.
All right, all good.
Our data set is well imported.
As you can see, it has 1000 observations.
That means that the cut between the review column and the liked column was done very properly without any issue.
cues.zh: 表示 Review 與 Liked 切分正確，沒有問題。

cues.en: So now let's open our data set and let's have a look.
As you can see all the reviews are very well separated to their verdict whether it's a positive or negative review.
cues.zh: 每則評論與正負判定都正確分開。

cues.en: And so everything here looks great and we need to make sure that we have our 1000 reviews.
cues.zh: 看來很好，也要確保一千則。

cues.en: Well, we can see that here very easily.
But you know, we have our 1000 reviews and when I scroll up, we can see that all the reviews are well in the review column.
cues.zh: 有一千則，往上捲，評論都在 Review 欄。

cues.en: And all the liked results 0 or 1 are well in the liked column here.
cues.zh: 0 或 1 都在 Liked 欄。

cues.en: You see if I scroll up, we don't have any review in the liked column or a one or zero in the review column.
cues.zh: 往上看，沒有評論跑進 Liked，也沒 1 或 0 跑到 Review。

cues.en: So everything looks great.
We are ready to move on to the next step which will be to clean the different reviews.
That is a compulsory step in Natural Language Processing which consists of cleaning the texts to make it ready for our future machine learning algorithms.
cues.zh: NLP 必要步驟，清理文字，為未來機器學習準備。

cues.en: So that's what we'll do in the next tutorial.
And until then, enjoy machine learning.
cues.zh: 在那之前，祝你享受機器學習的樂趣。
